reason: The cited evidence directly supports that Pd addition and annealing reduce FWHM (indicating reduced lattice distortions) and that this homogenization narrows the exchange energy distribution, leading to enhanced magnetocaloric properties. However, the evidence does not explicitly address the maintenance of rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, or mechanical stability, leaving those aspects of the premise unsupported.
premises: Pd addition and annealing reduce defect density and lattice distortions in NiFeCoCr-based HEAs
Reduced defect density and lattice distortions narrow the distribution of exchange energies
A narrower distribution of exchange energies sharpens the magnetic phase transition
A sharper magnetic phase transition enhances the magnetocaloric effect at low applied fields
Improved structural coherence maintains rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability
